searchText: <@592004585506340885> on naming: from our side it's a bit of a PITA to rename a devnet series after only one or two devnets. I'd prefer to keep <headliner>-devnet-N (carrying that layer's CFI'd EIPs) until we reach the merged phase, then switch to <fork>-devnet-N. That's what we did for Glamsterdam (bal-devnet-0..7 with the EL EIPs, epbs-devnet-0/1, then glamsterdam-devnet-0). Otherwise we end up with five tracks for one fork: focil, frames, heze, bogota, and hegota. So for Oct 28 that'd be focil-devnet-2 with FOCIL + 8015 + 8198 + 8365 (or whatever scope we decide). excerpts.content:
<@592004585506340885> on naming: from our side it's a bit of a PITA to rename a devnet series after only one or two devnets. I'd prefer to keep <headliner>-devnet-N (carrying that layer's CFI'd EIPs) until we reach the merged phase, then switch to <fork>-devnet-N. That's what we did for Glamsterdam (bal-devnet-0..7 with the EL EIPs, epbs-devnet-0/1, then glamsterdam-devnet-0). Otherwise we end up with five tracks for one fork: focil, frames, heze, bogota, and hegota.

So for Oct 28 that'd be focil-devnet-2 with FOCIL + 8015 + 8198 + 8365 (or whatever scope we decide). That said, I like the idea of using the fork name. For the next fork we could start straight away with <cl fork>-devnet-N and <el fork>-devnet-N instead of headliner names, and skip the renaming entirely, but would like to avoid for H* if possible.
